facts.fact: RFI reports that Angola's National Assembly adopted a cybersecurity law on 12 August 2026 by 104 votes (MPLA) to 56 (UNITA); the report does not say it was promulgated or in force.

note: No use of the law is stated; the report concerns the vote and criticism of vague wording.

facts.fact: PTI reports that the National Assembly approved the Cybersecurity Bill (Proposta de Lei da Cibersegurança) in global vote on 12 August 2026, 104 for, 54 against, no abstentions; the report does not say it was promulgated or in force.

note: No use of the law is stated.

facts.fact: ANGOP reports that the National Assembly adopted the cybersecurity law on 12 August 2026, 104 votes (MPLA) to 56 (UNITA), with fines of 7 to 4,000 national minimum wages by gravity; it does not say the law was promulgated or in force.

note: No use of the law is stated.

facts.fact: Novo Jornal reports that the National Assembly approved the Cybersecurity Bill in general terms on 23 January 2026, 105 for, 1 against and 75 UNITA abstentions.

A UNITA deputy, quoted by Novo Jornal, says Law 7/17 of 16 February (protection of computer networks and systems) is part of the current legal order and the bill would repeal it; the report dates nothing about Law 7/17 beyond its 2017 enactment, so as_of is the report's publication date.
